subject: gl.read.csv converting to silicodart not SNPs

messages.author: be5831679f44e5dc
messages.subject: gl.read.csv converting to silicodart not SNPs
parts:
Hey all,

When I try and read in a SNP dataset using gl.read.csv, it fails within the function at the line:

gl <- gl.recalc.metrics(gl) 

With this error:

Starting gl.read.csv
Warning: Locus metafile not provided, locus metrics will be
        calculated where this is possible
Input data should be a csv file with individuals as rows, loci as columns
   1146 loci, confirming first 5: loc1 loc2 loc3 loc4 loc5
   14 individuals, confirming first 5: EC6_Pseudomys_delicatulus_M48584_WA_CaneRiver EC6_Pseudomys_delicatulus_M48894_WA_PortHedland EC6_Pseudomys_delicatulus_M51961_WA_GiraliaSt EC6_Pseudomys_delicatulus_M51970_WA_GiraliaSt EC6_Pseudomys_hermannsburgensis_ABTC113867_QLD_Longreach
    If these are reversed, re-run the script with transpose=TRUE
Numeric data detected, assume genotypes are 0 = homozygous reference, 1 = heterozygous, 2 = homozygous alternate
Starting gl.recalc.metrics
  Processing  Presence/Absence (SilicoDArT) data
Starting utils.recalc.avgpic
  Processing  Presence/Absence (SilicoDArT) data, locus metric PIC
Error in if (x@other$loc.metrics.flags$monomorphs == FALSE) { :
  argument is of length zero
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In apply(data, 2, as.numeric) : NAs introduced by coercion
2: In apply(data, 2, as.numeric) : NAs introduced by coercion


For some reason, even though the data is coded 0/1/2, it thinks it is silicodart instead of SNPs. Any thoughts on why this could be happening?

Thanks,

Renee

Without having a look at the csv file (maybe you can send me it or part of it to reproduce.)

 

It looks like you have something else in your matrix as R creates NAs so maybe there are some characters in there. How do you code missing data?

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.read.csv converting to silicodart not SNPs
parts:
Hi Renee,

The problem was that ploidy and flags are not set when reading csv files. Please find attached the fixed function.

Because google groups doesn't allow to send executable files, the attached file has a ".txt" extension. To use this function please save it to your working directory and change the extension of the file to ".R". Then in the command line of R type:

> library(dartR)
> source("gl.read.csv.R")
> test <- gl.read.csv("your_data.csv")

Please let us know whether it worked for you.

Regards,
Luis
